name: Doubled c-pawns (Nimzo family, White pair)

plans.label: Roll the centre
plans.description: The doubled pawn bought an extra central pawn and the bishop pair: build the broad centre with the e- and f-pawns and advance it before the c4 pawn becomes the story.

success.note: The central duo stands on d4 and e4; whether it is strength or target is not arithmetic.

plans.label: Open lines for the bishops
plans.description: The defect's other dividend: use the half-open b-file and the two bishops in an opening position before the structure is fixed against you.

success.note: Line quality for the bishop pair is not expressible as pawn arithmetic.

plans.label: Fix the pawns
plans.description: Restrain the front pawn with a pawn planted on c5 so neither c-pawn can ever move, accepting the d5 hole that the clamp concedes.

success.note: A Black pawn on c5 stands in front of the still-doubled pair with c4 fixed in place.

plans.label: Besiege the front pawn
plans.description: Blockade in front of the pair and pile pieces on the fixed front pawn - the knight-to-the-rim manoeuvre toward a5 is the classic route.

success.note: The front pawn fell rather than advanced: c3 survives while c4 and c5 hold no White pawn.

plans.label: Keep it closed
plans.description: Deny the bishop pair open lines; a blocked position turns the doubled pawns back into a plain weakness.

success.note: Closedness has no arithmetic definition in this vocabulary.

watch: The attacker and defender counts on c4 once it is fixed.
Whether the position opens for the bishops or stays closed for the knights.
The d5 square from the moment Black commits a pawn to c5.
typicalMistakes: Winning the c4 pawn at the price of opening every line for the bishop pair.
Rolling the centre forward before the king is safe.
Releasing the clamp on c5 to win material and letting the front pawn advance at last.

Trigger narrowing: the doubled-and-backward family in the content map spans the Nimzo White c-pawns, the Ruy Lopez Exchange Black c-pawns, and the Sveshnikov backward d-pawn; one entry cannot carry all three because the plan sides reverse per case. This entry encodes only the White-owned Nimzo pair with the front pawn on c4 and the b-file half-open; the Black-owned mirrors remain unauthored.
